literal: Virtue without-failing, non-virtuous-things having-removed, valor unfailing honor that-which-possesses [is] king.
translation: A true king is one who never fails in virtue, eradicates evil, and possesses honor backed by unfailing valor.
modern: அறத்திலிருந்து தவறாமல், தீயவற்றை நாட்டை விட்டு நீக்கி, வீரத்தில் குறையாத மானத்தை உடையதே சிறந்த அரசாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the essential qualities of a good ruler. A king must steadfastly uphold virtue and actively eradicate evil from his realm. Furthermore, he must possess a deep sense of honor that is backed by unwavering courage. The words for virtue and valor are paired to show that moral righteousness and martial strength must coexist to protect the state.
